proposals.before: They seized the supply train and advanced on Jinan.
proposals.after: They seized the supply train and advanced on Jining.
proposals.reason: Chinese 濟寧 is Jining, not Jinan (濟南); the idiomatic rendering names the wrong city.

proposals.before: They plundered the baggage train and pressed forward toward Jinan.
proposals.after: They plundered the baggage train and pressed forward toward Jining.
proposals.reason: Chinese 進薄濟寧 refers to Jining; the literal English invents Jinan.

proposals.before: The next day they fought again: the Yan army on the northeast, Yong's army on the southwest; from the seventh to the second hour of the afternoon, victory seesawed.
proposals.after: The next day they fought again: the Yan army on the northeast, Yong's army on the southwest; from the chen hour to the wei hour, victory seesawed.
proposals.reason: 辰至未 runs from early morning (chen) to early afternoon (wei); the literal rendering misreads the double-hour labels.

proposals.before: He marched with Chang Yuchun against the Yuan capital and was killed in action.
proposals.after: He marched with Chang Yuchun to take the Yuan capital and was killed in action.
proposals.reason: 下元都 means capturing or taking the Yuan capital, not merely campaigning against it.

proposals.before: Soon after he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Palace.
proposals.after: Soon after he was promoted to vice commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Military Commission.
proposals.reason: 後府 here is the Rear Chief Military Commission (後軍都督府), not a palace office.

proposals.before: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Palace.
proposals.after: Shortly thereafter he was advanced to Vice Commissioner-in-chief of the Rear Military Commission.
proposals.reason: 後府 denotes the Rear Military Commission, not the palace.

proposals.before: In the third month of Yongle 7 the emperor toured Beiping.
proposals.after: In the third month of Yongle 7 the emperor toured Beijing.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is 北京 (Beijing), the Yongle-era name, not Beiping.

proposals.before: In the third month of the seventh year of Yongle the Emperor toured Beiping.
proposals.after: In the third month of the seventh year of Yongle the Emperor toured Beijing.
proposals.reason: The Chinese is 北京, not 北平.

proposals.before: The next year, in the first month, He Fu and Vice Commissioner Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Zhulu and Yan, and wiped them out.
proposals.after: The next year, in the first month, He Fu and Commissioner-in-chief Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Fu and Yan, and wiped them out.
proposals.reason: 鄜 is Fu (Fuzhou), not Zhulu; 都督 is commissioner-in-chief rather than specifically vice commissioner.

proposals.before: In the first month of the following year Fu and Vice Commissioner Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Zhulu and Yan, and annihilated them completely.
proposals.after: In the first month of the following year Fu and Commissioner-in-chief Nie Wei pursued them, caught them at Fu and Yan, and annihilated them completely.
proposals.reason: 鄜 is Fu, not Zhulu; 都督 is not Vice Commissioner.

proposals.before: By then the founding emperor was dead and the new emperor had just taken the throne; He Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
proposals.after: By then the founding emperor was dead and the Hui Emperor had just taken the throne; He Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
proposals.reason: 惠帝 is the Hui Emperor (Jianwen), not merely an unnamed new emperor.

proposals.before: At that time the founding emperor had died and the Huandi had just taken the throne; Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
proposals.after: At that time the founding emperor had died and the Huidi had just taken the throne; Fu was appointed General for the Punishment of Barbarians.
proposals.reason: Huandi is a mistransliteration of 惠帝; the established form is Huidi.

proposals.before: He betrothed Fu's niece, the Xu clan, as Princess of Zhao.
proposals.after: He betrothed Fu's niece, née Xu, as consort of the Prince of Zhao.
proposals.reason: 徐氏 is the niece's surname, not an equation of the niece with the Xu clan; 趙王妃 is consort of the Prince of Zhao.

proposals.before: He marched on Shu, attacked Luojiang, captured the Yuan commander and more than twenty officers under him, and advanced to accept Hanzhou's surrender.
proposals.after: He marched on Shu, attacked Luojiang, captured the enemy commander-in-chief and more than twenty officers under him, and advanced to accept Hanzhou's surrender.
proposals.reason: Chinese 元帥 is a military office, not the Yuan dynasty; Yuan commander invents a dynasty identification the source does not make.

proposals.before: It happened that He Fu campaigned against the Shuixi tribes and beheaded the chieftain Juzong Bideng.
proposals.after: It happened that He Fu campaigned against the Shuixi tribes; Cheng beheaded the chieftain Juzong Bideng.
proposals.reason: The biography silent subject of beheading is still Gu Cheng; 會 marks coincidence with He Fu campaign, not a change of agent.

proposals.before: The next year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; he sent Commander Lu Bing and his son Tong by separate routes to put them down.
proposals.after: The next year the tribes of Xibao, Canglang, and other stockades rebelled; he sent Commander Lu Bing and Cheng's son Tong by separate routes to put them down.
proposals.reason: 其子統 is Gu Cheng's son 統, later named as his eldest, not Lu Bing's son; English his after Lu Bing misassigns the kinship.

proposals.before: Sinzhou Pacification Commissioner Tian Chen and Sinan Pacification Commissioner Tian Zongding raised troops against one another; an edict ordered Gu Cheng to press their borders with fifty thousand troops, and Chen and the others were captured.
proposals.after: Sizhou Pacification Commissioner Tian Chen and Sinan Pacification Commissioner Tian Zongding raised troops against one another; an edict ordered Gu Cheng to press their borders with fifty thousand troops, and Chen and the others were captured.
proposals.reason: 思州 is Sizhou, matching the next sentence; Sinzhou is an inconsistent romanization.

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Grand Mentor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
proposals.reason: 太傅 is Grand Mentor/Grand Tutor, not Grand Preceptor (太師).

proposals.before: He was posthumously made Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
proposals.after: He was posthumously made Grand Mentor with the posthumous title Rongxi.
proposals.reason: 太傅 is Grand Mentor/Grand Tutor, not Grand Preceptor (太師).

decisions.reason: The source names 濟寧, not 濟南; Jinan is a different city and the replacement restores the correct place.
進薄濟寧 is an advance on Jining; the literal English wrongly substitutes Jinan.
自辰至未 names the chen and wei double-hours (morning to early afternoon); 'the seventh to the second hour of the afternoon' misreads those labels.
下元都 means taking the Yuan capital, not merely campaigning against it; the replacement matches 下 and the unit's own literal.
行後府 is the Rear Chief Military Commission, not a palace; Palace invents a civil household office the Chinese does not name.
後府 in 都督僉事 is the rear military commission; Rear Palace is a mistranslation of 府.
The tour destination is 北京, distinct from 北平 in the preceding appointment; Beiping is the wrong toponym here.
The Chinese is 北京, not 北平; the literal must follow the named place.
鄜 is Fu, not Zhulu, and 都督 is commissioner-in-chief rather than vice commissioner (都督僉事); both replacements restore the source.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 福與都督聶緯追擊，及諸鄜、延

decisions.reason: The same clause has 都督 and 鄜、延; Vice Commissioner and Zhulu are not in the Chinese.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 都督聶緯追擊，及諸鄜、延

decisions.reason: 惠帝 is a specific ruler-name, not a generic new emperor; the replacement restores the omitted designation.
惠帝 romanizes as Huidi; Huandi would be 桓帝 and is a naming error.
徐氏 marks the niece as née Xu, and 趙王妃 is consort of the Prince of Zhao, not a princess and not 'the Xu clan' as the person.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 聘其甥女徐氏為趙王妃

decisions.reason: 元帥 is a military rank; reading it as Yuan dynasty invents a polity the Shu campaign sentence does not name.

何福 is the expressed subject of 討, and 斬其酋 continues that verb chain; 會 marks the occasion, while the next sentence reintroduces 成, so inserting Cheng as the beheader is not required and may misattribute the killing.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 會何福討水西蠻，斬其酋居宗必登

decisions.reason: 成遣…與其子統 makes 其 Cheng's son 統, not Lu Bing's; the English 'his' after Lu Bing misassigns kinship.

sourceWitness.excerpt: 成遣指揮陸秉與其子統分道討平之

decisions.reason: 思州 is Sizhou, as in the next sentence's 思州、思南; Sinzhou is a wrong romanization of the same place.
太傅 is Grand Mentor, distinct from Grand Preceptor 太師.
The same 太傅 requires Grand Mentor in the literal field as well.
